Threads: 64 (654.98us) and 256 (474.98us) both regressed, so fix threads=[128]. stages=3 regressed at 64x64 (524.35us), so keep num_stages=[2,3] biased to s2. block_N=64 drove the slow attempt-08, so restrict to [128,256]. To test the still-unexplored large-M hypothesis, expand block_M to [64,128,256] (256 divides M=4096 and may raise per-SM work while keeping swizzle panel reuse meaningful); keep block_K=[32,64] to test deeper-K at the winning tile, and swizzle [8,16,32] to bracket the winner. Note smem estimate 4*block_M*block_N=4*256*256=262144 > cap so 256x256 is pruned by HiGHS; 128x256 footprint 131072 also infeasible, steering toward feasible large-M/moderate-N combos. Next hypothesis: block_M=128 (or 256) with block_N=128/256, block_K=32/64, stages=2, threads=128, swizzle 8-32 lowers latency below 399.54us. Validation scope: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed."}
